Attempt to hold a user in another company, and to hold another **administrator**, and confirm the service refuses. This route also writes **no audit row**, so a suspension leaves no trace in the audit trail - worth flagging given it is a user-impacting action.

**Note on recent changes.** Git history shows a commit titled "holdOrRelease api query busniess condition removed", indicating a business rule was recently stripped from this path - regression coverage here is worth prioritising.

post.summary: Suggest a display name from company and designation
post.description:
Derives a proposed display name by combining a company name with a designation - the label shown to other users alongside an employee's messages and in the directory. Used to pre-fill the display-name field during provisioning, complementing `createKpostIDAndDesignationSuggestion`, which suggests the identity itself.

**Flow.** `companyName` and `designation` are read from the untyped request map and passed to `SignUpLoginService.displayNameSuggestion`, which composes and returns a candidate name - potentially checking it against existing display names in MySQL for uniqueness. An audit row is written.

**Side effects.** None - nothing is persisted and the suggested name is not reserved.

Worth checking how the service handles very long company names or designations containing punctuation, since the result is user-visible.

post.summary: Grant or revoke backup-administrator rights
post.description:
Promotes a user to backup administrator, or demotes them - the continuity control that ensures a company is not locked out of administration if the primary admin is unavailable.

**Flow.** The acting admin's `kpostID` is read from the bearer token and passed to `SignUpLoginService.createOrRemoveBackupAdmin` alongside the target user, so the service can enforce that the caller is entitled to delegate. The backup-admin flag is set or cleared on the target's row in MySQL, and the granted role is what subsequently lets that user pass the `hasRole("admin")` gate on this whole tree. The response message is chosen from `isBackUpAdmin` in the **request**, not from the service result.

**Side effects - privilege change.** Granting gives the target full access to every `/admin/**` route, including the ability to provision, suspend and terminate users. Revoking removes it. This is the platform's privilege-delegation mechanism and should be covered carefully.

**Access.** Requires the `admin` role. Writes an audit row.

**QA notes.** Key cases: confirm a newly-granted backup admin can immediately reach `/admin/**` routes (and whether they must re-authenticate for the role to take effect in their token); confirm a revoked admin is refused with **403**; and confirm an admin cannot grant rights to a user in another company. Note the **null-pointer risk**: `user.getIsBackUpAdmin()` is unboxed with `==` on the success path, so omitting `isBackUpAdmin` from the payload throws an NPE that is caught and returned as the generic HTTP 500 - always send the flag explicitly. Also note the message is derived from the request rather than the persisted state, so a response saying "Backup Admin added Successfully" reflects what was asked for, not necessarily what the service did; verify by re-reading the user.

post.summary: Suggest a kpostID and designation for a new employee
post.description:
Generates a proposed `kpostID` from the company name and designation, together with a suggested designation label - the helper the admin console calls to pre-fill the provisioning form before `addingUserByAdmin` is submitted.

**Flow.** An `AdminRegistration` is assembled from the payload's `companyName` and `designation`, and `user.kpostID` is **overwritten with the acting admin's id from the bearer token**. `CommonService.generateKpostId` then derives a candidate id (returned lower-cased), while `SignUpLoginService.checkExistingDesignationAndSuggestion` proposes a designation - falling back to the designation supplied in the request when it has no better suggestion. An audit row is written.

**Side effects.** None - nothing is persisted and the suggested id is **not reserved**, so it can be taken by another provisioning request before `addingUserByAdmin` runs. Expect occasional collisions at provisioning time.

Assert that the returned `kpostID` is lower-case, and that `designationSuggestion` echoes your input when no alternative exists. Envelope keys are `kpostID` and `designationSuggestion` at the top level, not under `data`, and `urlPath` is reported as `createIdAndDestinationSuggestion` - which matches neither the route nor the method name.

post.summary: Reallocate an existing kpostID to a new employee
post.description:
Assigns a `kpostID` that was previously held by a departed employee to a new person - the reallocation path that lets a company reuse role-based identities (for example `sales.head@acme`) as staff change, preserving the identity while replacing the human behind it.

**Flow.** The acting admin's `kpostID` is stamped from the bearer token and an audit row written. `SignUpLoginService.addingUserForReallocateByAdmin` then rebinds the existing `kpostID` in MySQL to the new person's details rather than allocating a fresh one, and re-issues credentials.

**Side effects - the most consequential in this controller.** The new holder inherits an identity that already exists in other users' contact lists, group memberships and message histories. Depending on how the service handles retention, the incoming employee may gain visibility of the previous holder's Katchup threads, Kmail and stored attachments. **This is a data-protection concern worth testing directly**: reallocate an id that has message history and confirm what the new user can see. Any live sessions belonging to the previous holder should also be revoked - verify that their old token no longer authenticates.

Note the failure envelope reports `urlPath` as `addingUserByAdmin` - a copy-paste artefact, so the response cannot be used to identify which of the two routes failed.

post.summary: Provision a new employee account
post.description:
Creates a KPOST account for a member of the administrator's company - the primary staff-onboarding action.

**Flow.** The acting admin's `kpostID` is read from the bearer token and stamped onto `userRegistration.admin`, so the audit trail records who provisioned the account and the payload cannot spoof it. An audit row is written, then `SignUpLoginService.addingUserByAdmin` validates uniqueness, allocates the `kpostID`, and inserts the user, profile, company-membership and default-settings rows into MySQL. **Side effects.** Creates a real account and typically dispatches onboarding credentials to the employee by SMS/email - **outward-facing consequences for a third party**, so use test contact details. Consumes a seat against the company's licensed user count.

**QA notes.** Contrast `POST /signupLoginForMediumAndLarge/addingUserByAdmin`, which is **unauthenticated** and does not record the acting admin - that route is the security-relevant one; this is the correct, gated equivalent. The payload carries `@Valid`, so bean-validation failures produce a genuine **400** via `GlobalExceptionHandler`. Test cross-company provisioning: supply a `companyID` the admin does not belong to and confirm the service refuses. Duplicate identities and seat-limit breaches both collapse into the generic HTTP 500 with `errorValue="Error occurred while trying to Adding User!"`, so read the service's message to distinguish them.

get.summary: Log out of every device
get.description:
Terminates all live sessions for the signed-in user at once - the "sign out everywhere" control, and the primary remedy when an account is suspected compromised or a device is lost.

**Flow.** The `kpostID` is resolved from the bearer token. If it is null the handler returns a genuine **HTTP 401** with `errorMsg="Authentication failed or token is missing"` - this is the only route in the controller that performs its own authentication check, which matters because the `/v2/signupLogin/**` tree is `permitAll` and the filter chain will not do it. Otherwise a `LogoutRO` is built from the token identity and `SignUpLoginService.userLogoutFromAllDevices` deletes every session row for that user from MySQL. An audit row is written.

**Side effects.** Bulk-deletes session rows. Every outstanding token - **including the caller's own** - stops authenticating immediately, so the client must discard its token and return to the login screen. Irreversible; every device must sign in again.

**Security improvement over V1.** The V1 equivalent took the target `kpostID` from the request body with no ownership check, allowing one user to forcibly sign out another. This route accepts **no parameters at all** and derives the subject solely from the token, so that abuse is structurally impossible.

**QA notes.** This is a **GET that performs a destructive bulk write**, so it is prefetchable and cacheable by intermediaries - avoid placing it in link-like contexts. Key assertions: call it with no token and expect **401**; then, after a successful call, reuse tokens from two separate devices and expect 401 on both, and confirm `getActiveSession` returns the empty case. Also verify that a refresh token from a revoked session can no longer mint a new access token via `generateJWTokens` - if it can, logout is ineffective.

200.description: All sessions terminated. Envelope carries `status=Success`, `statusCode=200` and `msg="You have been logged out from all devices successfully"`.

get.description:
Returns the live device sessions for the signed-in user - the "logged in devices" screen that lets someone review which devices hold a valid token and spot access they do not recognise.

**Flow.** `SignUpLoginService.getActiveSession` selects the live rows from the MySQL login-session table for the `kpostID` resolved from the bearer token, returning device ids, device names and login timestamps under `data`. An audit row is written.

get.summary: [Public] Fetch attachment metadata or link by UUID
get.description:
Resolves an attachment UUID to its stored details. Unlike the sibling download routes this returns a **JSON envelope** rather than raw bytes - typically the file metadata and/or a URL the client then fetches.

**Access - public, and this one carries private data.** `/v2/katchup/downloadAttachment/**` is listed as `permitAll` in `SecurityConfiguration`, so **no bearer token is required**. Attachments are private message content - photographs, documents, voice notes exchanged between two people - so an unauthenticated route keyed only on a UUID means **possession of the UUID is the only access control**. That is defensible if UUIDs are random and never leak, but QA should establish: (1) that UUIDs are genuinely version-4 random and not sequential or derivable; (2) whether UUIDs appear in logs, referrer headers or client-side URLs where they could leak; and (3) whether a recalled or deleted message's attachment is still retrievable here - if it is, recall does not actually revoke access to the file. **Report the outcome of (3) regardless**, since it determines whether recall is meaningful for attachments.

**Side effects.** None - read-only.

**QA notes.** Compare the five download variants - `downloadAttachment` (this, JSON), `oldDownload` (bytes, legacy), `downloadFromS3` (JSON), `download` (wildcard type) and `downloadThumbnail` (bytes) - and establish which the client should use; maintaining five is itself worth flagging.

get.summary: Verify that a single attachment uploaded to S3 successfully
get.description:
Confirms whether the direct-to-S3 PUT actually landed, which the client calls after uploading and before referencing the UUID in a message. `PreSignedURLService.checkAttachmentS3` inspects the caller's namespace in the configured bucket and returns one of four sentinel values, each of which this handler maps to a **distinct HTTP status** - this is the most granular status mapping in the codebase and is the main thing to get right when testing:

| Service result | HTTP | `msg` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Success` | **200** | Attachment Uploaded Successfully | Object present; safe to reference. |
| `Invalid_user` | **406** | UUID is not belongs to the user | The UUID exists but is outside the caller's namespace. |
| `Failure` | **417** | Folder created but Attachment not Uploaded | Prefix exists, object missing - the PUT did not complete. |
| `no_folder` | **404** | Folder not created and Attachment not Uploaded | Nothing was written at all. |
| anything else | **404** | exception occurred while checking | Unexpected service outcome. |

**Side effects.** Writes an audit row; otherwise read-only against S3.

**QA notes.** Note the route spelling: `checkAttachmenS3` is **missing the second `t`** in "Attachment" and must be reproduced exactly, whereas the batch POST sibling is spelled correctly as `checkAttachmentS3`. The 406 branch is the authorisation case worth covering explicitly. An unhandled exception returns HTTP 500 with an **empty envelope**, so do not assume `status` is always present. Because eventual consistency can briefly hide a fresh object, allow a short retry window before treating 417 as a genuine upload failure.

get.summary: Check whether a booking was actually ticketed
get.description: Reconciliation call that reports whether a given booking reference resulted in a confirmed ticket at RedBus. Its main purpose is recovering from ambiguity: if `bookticket` times out or the client loses connectivity mid-confirmation, this tells the client whether the ticket exists **before** it considers retrying - which is what prevents duplicate bookings. The handler checks the booking against the RedBus partner API through `SSRestServiceClient` and reports the result in the standard envelope. Side effects: none - read-only against upstream. QA notes: **this route is declared with a bare `@RequestMapping`, so it responds to every HTTP method**, not just POST; a GET will fail body binding. The scenario to test is the interrupted-booking path: block, confirm, kill the connection, then use this endpoint to establish the true state. Note the trailing slash in the route.

kpostID.description: The account whose session is ended. Ignored and overwritten from the bearer token on the V2 route.

deviceType.description: Platform of the device being signed out.

deviceIdentity_primary.description: Identifier of the device session to terminate. Must match the `deviceID` claim carried in the token issued to that device.

logoutTime.description: Client-reported logout timestamp, recorded in the login history.

remarks.description: Optional free-text note stored against the logout record.

module.description: Numeric module identifier indicating which product the logout originated from.

LogoutRO.description: Logout payload for the session-termination routes. On `POST /v2/signupLogin/userLogout` the `kpostID` is **overwritten from the bearer token**, so only the device fields influence which session is ended.

deviceIdentity_primary.description: **Effectively mandatory.** The stable per-installation device identifier. It is embedded in the JWT as the `deviceID` claim and matched against the login-session table on every request, so a token minted without it cannot authenticate anything.

deviceIdentity_secondary.description: Secondary device identifier, where the platform supplies two.

logintime.description: Client-reported sign-in time, recorded in the login history read back by `getLoginHistory`.

login_lattitude.description: Latitude captured at sign-in. **Location data** - confirm it is genuinely needed, that the user consented, and that it is not exposed through any read endpoint.

login_longitude.description: Longitude captured at sign-in. Same privacy considerations as the latitude.

oneSignal_Key.description: OneSignal push registration key for this device, used to deliver notifications.

socketID.description: Socket identifier for the real-time channel.

module.description: Numeric product identifier indicating which client is signing in. Defaults to 0 (KPOST Flutter).

voip.description: VoIP push token, used to raise the incoming-call screen for Kall. If this is stale, calls are recorded correctly but the device never rings - the most common cause of a false Kall defect.

LoginSession.description: Login payload and session record. Sent to `POST /v2/signupLogin/userLogin`; the fields below both authenticate the user and define the **device-bound session** that the resulting JWT is tied to. `AuthenticationFilter` matches the token's `deviceID` claim against this session on every subsequent request, so a token only authenticates while its session is alive.

statusCode.description: Service-level status code, mirroring the HTTP status: 200 on success, 400 for a validation failure, 500 for a rejected login or a fault.

message.description: Human-readable outcome. Note that rejected credentials and genuine server faults both report `API service is not working`, so this message does **not** distinguish a wrong password from an outage - assert on the absence of `accessToken` instead.

urlPath.description: Echoes the route that produced the response. Informational only.

accessToken.description: The JWT access token. Send it on every authenticated call as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. It carries `kpostID`, `deviceID` and `companyID` claims, and is **device-bound** - it authenticates only while the matching login-session row is alive, so it stops working after logout from that device.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token, exchanged for a new access token via `POST /v2/signupLogin/generateJWTokens`. Longer-lived than the access token and therefore **as sensitive as a password** - it is the sole credential on that exchange.

isFirstTimeLogin.description: True when this is the user's first ever sign-in, letting the client run onboarding - for example prompting for an access code or profile completion.

isPrimaryDevice.description: True when the signing-in device is the account's primary device. The primary device is authoritative for Kmail and certain privileged operations, so the client uses this to decide whether to expose those features.

isSecondaryDeviceFirstTimeLogin.description: True when this is the first sign-in from a device newly designated secondary, so the client can run the reduced secondary-device onboarding.

isSecondaryDevice.description: True when the signing-in device is designated a secondary (companion) device, which carries a reduced set of Kmail privileges relative to the primary.

data.description: The authenticated user summary - typically a `SignUpLoginResponseObject` carrying `kpostID`, display name and `companyID`. Absent when the login was rejected.

additionalProperties.description: The user's stored theme and personalisation settings, returned at login so the client can paint the correct appearance without a follow-up call to `generalSetting/getPersonalize`.

changeTheme.description: The user's stored theme and personalisation settings, returned at login so the client can paint the correct appearance without a follow-up call to `generalSetting/getPersonalize`.

LoginApiResponse.description: The authentication response envelope, returned by `POST /v2/signupLogin/userLogin` and `POST /signupLoginForMediumAndLarge/adminUserLogin`. Extends the standard envelope with the JWT pair and the device-state flags the client needs to decide what to show immediately after sign-in. **Handle the token fields as credentials**: store them in secure storage, never log them, and never place them in a URL.

kpostID.description: The KPOST identity, in `local@domain` form. Overwritten from the bearer token on most authenticated routes.

firstName.description: Given name. Mandatory on the kpostID availability and suggestion routes, which skip their lookup entirely if it is absent.

lastName.description: Family name. Mandatory alongside `firstName` on the suggestion routes.

mobileNumber.description: Mobile number in national format, digits only.

accessCode.description: The short secondary PIN that unlocks the app and authorises sensitive actions.

requestType.description: Discriminator letting one payload serve several flows, for example distinguishing a password reset from a kpostID reminder.

oldPassword.description: The existing password, required when changing it.

confirmPassword.description: Repeat of the new password for client-side confirmation.

currentPassword.description: Alternative name for the existing password; check which the target endpoint reads.

companyName.description: Company display name, used by the company lookup and suggestion routes.

designation.description: Job designation, ideally drawn from the reference catalogue exposed by `/v2/common/getDesignation`.

userType.description: Account tier. `PERSONAL` triggers the 4-12 character local-part rule on sign-up.

accountNumber.description: Bank account number. **Financially sensitive** - confirm it is masked on read-back and never written to logs.

bankName.description: Bank name for the settlement account.

productId.description: Product identifier, used by `getCompanyDetailsByMobileNoAndproductId` to filter companies to those licensed for a given product.

UserRO.description: General-purpose user payload, reused across sign-up, profile, admin and company routes. **Only a subset of these fields is read by any given endpoint** - the rest are ignored - so consult the individual operation description for which ones matter. Several routes overwrite `kpostID` from the bearer token; where they do not, the operation says so explicitly.

kpostID.description: The account the tokens belong to.

password.description: Account password. Not normally needed for a refresh exchange - the refresh token is the credential - so confirm with the service whether supplying it changes behaviour.

accessToken.description: The expired or expiring access token being replaced.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token presented in exchange for a new access token. Must be unexpired **and** its device session still live - one whose session was revoked by logout must be rejected.

TokenRO.description: Token-exchange payload for `POST /v2/signupLogin/generateJWTokens`, which mints a fresh access token from a valid refresh token so the user need not sign in again. **All fields here are credentials** - never log this payload or place it in a URL.

statusCode.description: Service-level status code. Usually mirrors the HTTP status, but some endpoints deliberately or accidentally differ - see the operation description.

status.description: Outcome indicator. Normally `Success` or `Failure`; a few controllers also use `Error` for caught exceptions, and the AI module uses uppercase variants.

message.description: Human-readable outcome message. On failures this carries the reason; on successes it is often a short confirmation or a label describing the payload.

urlPath.description: Echoes the route that produced the response. Informational only - it is inconsistent across the codebase and sometimes reports the handler method name or a stale path rather than the actual route, so do not use it for dispatch.

data.description: The response payload. Its type varies by endpoint - an object, an array, or a plain string - and it is **absent on most failures**, so assert on its presence rather than on `status` when checking whether a call really succeeded.

ApiResponse.description: The platform's standard typed response envelope, used by the V2 controllers. Every field except `data` is always present. **Note for QA:** several endpoints return a `statusCode` in this body that does not match the HTTP status of the response - the individual operation descriptions call out where that happens. Where they disagree, treat the body's `statusCode` as the service's intent and the HTTP status as the transport result.

kpostID.description: The profile being read or written. Overwritten from the bearer token on the V2 routes; taken from this payload on the V1 routes.

requestType.description: Discriminator letting one payload serve several flows.

country.description: Country name for the address block.

state.description: State or region, ideally matching a value from `/v2/common/getStates`.

city.description: City, ideally matching `/v2/common/getCitiesByRegionId` for the chosen region.

alternateMobileno.description: Secondary contact number. Note that changing a **primary** number is security-relevant, since it is the account-recovery channel.

UserProfileRO.description: Profile payload covering the contact, address, education and experience sections. Reused widely across `/profile` and `/v2/profile`, so **only a subset is read by any given endpoint**. On the V2 routes the target user is resolved from the bearer token; on the V1 routes it is taken from `kpostID` in this payload with no ownership check - see the individual operation descriptions.

kpostID.description: The member being acted on, or the caller on the self-service routes. Overwritten from the bearer token where the operation says so.

kpostIDs.description: Several members, for the batch operations.

items.description: Several members, for the batch operations.

groupAdmin.description: The acting administrator. Ignored and overwritten from the bearer token.

hasAdminAccess.description: Admin delegation flag, compared by **exact match** on `"Y"` (grant) or `"N"` (revoke). Any other value, including lowercase, takes the fallthrough branch. Mandatory - omitting it causes a NullPointerException on the V1 route.

groupKpostID.description: The group's stable identifier. Must **not** change when the group is renamed - a changing identifier would break clients' local databases and stored message references.

memberKpostIdList.description: Members to add or remove in a batch operation.

items.description: Members to add or remove in a batch operation.

groupKpostName.description: The group's display name, set at creation and changed via `editGroupName`.

remarks.description: Optional free-text note recorded against the operation.

UserGroupRO.description: Group-operation payload for `/group` and `/v2/group`. The acting user is always stamped from the bearer token - `groupAdmin` on the admin-facing routes, `kpostID` on `leaveFromGroup` and `deleteGroup` - so the payload cannot spoof who is acting. What the service must still enforce is that the actor administers the target group.

lastMsgID.description: Paging cursor - return only messages newer than this id. Send 0 for the first page.

msgID.description: Identifier of a single message, used by the recall, delete and reference routes.

sender.description: The message author. Overwritten from the bearer token on the authenticated send routes.

receiver.description: The recipient - either a contact kpostID or a group kpostID, which triggers fan-out to every member.

messageType.description: Message semantics as an integer: 0 normal, 1 reply, 2 share, 3 reminder, 4 SMS, 5 note, 6 edit, 7 recall, 8 comment, 9 clarify, 11 group notification, 15 forward, 17 schedule-Kall notification, 25 share document.

actualMessage.example: Running 20 minutes late for the inspection.

deviceID.description: Originating device identifier, matching the `deviceID` claim in the bearer token.

subject.description: Subject line. Katchup threads messages by subject, so this determines which thread the message joins.

referenceMsgID.description: The message this one replies to, shares or forwards - the link the reference and back-track routes walk.

receiverList.description: Recipients for the bulk send routes. **High fan-out** - one request delivers to every entry and raises a push notification for each.

items.description: Recipients for the bulk send routes. **High fan-out** - one request delivers to every entry and raises a push notification for each.

secretMessageExpireTime.description: Expiry for a disappearing message. Verify the message genuinely becomes unreadable afterwards, including via search and the attachment routes.

KatchupMessageRO.description: The Katchup message payload, used for sending, forwarding and bulk delivery. **`sender` is always overwritten from the bearer token** on the `/v2/katchup` routes, so authorship cannot be spoofed there - the exception is `POST /v2/common/sendMessage`, which reads it from this payload on an unauthenticated route.

sender.description: The caller side of the conversation. Overwritten from the bearer token, so a user cannot read a thread they are not part of by altering it.

receiver.description: The other party - a contact kpostID, or a group kpostID when `groupFlag` is set.

groupFlag.description: True when `receiver` names a group rather than an individual.

msgID.description: Target message for the single-message actions - recall, delete, flag.

markFlag.description: Desired important/starred state for `markOrUnmarkImportantMessage`. The flag is private to the caller and must not be visible to the other party.

searchMessage.description: Free-text search term. Results must be restricted to the caller's own conversations.

messageIds.description: Batch of message ids for the multi-message actions. Confirm each is authorised individually rather than the batch as a whole.

items.description: Batch of message ids for the multi-message actions. Confirm each is authorised individually rather than the batch as a whole.

lastMsgID.description: Paging cursor - return only messages newer than this id. Send 0 for the first page.

selectedContact.description: The contact whose conversation subjects are being listed.

FetchKatchupRO.description: Message-retrieval and message-action payload for the Katchup module. Serves the thread fetch, search, recall, delete and flag routes; only the fields relevant to each are read. `sender` is overwritten from the bearer token on the routes that receive the request, anchoring the conversation to the caller.

kallID.description: Call identifier. **Sequential**, so treat it as enumerable when testing authorisation on the status and info reads.

sender.description: The call originator. Resolved from the bearer token on the authenticated routes.

kallMode.description: Call medium - distinguishes voice from video. Confirm the accepted values with the service.

senderKallStatus.description: The originator's side of the call state - ringing, answered, declined, ended.

kallType.description: Call category, for example direct versus scheduled versus recurring.

kallSession.description: Session identifier tying this signalling record to the media session on the VoIP path.

meetingLink.description: Join URL for the call, where one is issued.

scheduledStartTime.description: Planned start for a scheduled call. Confirm this is stored unambiguously (UTC or with an explicit offset) - a naive local time fires reminders at the wrong moment for participants in other zones.

scheduledEndTime.description: Planned end for a scheduled call.

repeatType.description: Recurrence pattern for `scheduledRepeatKall` - daily, weekly and so on.

repeatDate.description: Recurrence detail, such as the days of the week a weekly series falls on.

receiver.description: The callee, or a group identifier for a multi-party call.

receiverKallStatus.description: The callee's side of the call state.

reason.description: Free-text reason recorded when declining or ending a call.

selectedDate.description: Date filter for the scheduled-call reads.

KallROV3.description: The V3 call payload used across `/v2/kall`. Carries both direct-call and scheduled-call fields; only the subset relevant to each route is read. The acting user is always resolved from the bearer token - a deliberate correction of V1, where several call routes took no caller identity at all.

lastfetchDate.description: Sync cursor - return only records changed since this instant. **Mandatory on the listing routes**: omitting it does not trigger a full fetch, it skips the query and yields the empty response. Note the casing difference - this request field is `lastfetchDate` (lowercase f) while the response field is `lastFetchDate` (capital F).

contactIDs.description: The contacts to act on, used by the bulk block/unblock route. Ignored by the listing routes.

items.description: The contacts to act on, used by the bulk block/unblock route. Ignored by the listing routes.

isBlocked.description: Block state applied to **every** contact in `contactIDs` - `true` to block, `false` to unblock. Being a single value for the whole batch, one request cannot mix blocks and unblocks.

ContactsRO.description: Dual-purpose payload for the `/v2/contacts` module: it carries the **sync cursor** for the four incremental listing routes (`myContacts`, `myUnknownKatchupContacts`, `myGroups`, `myUnknownGroups`) and the **batch selection** for `blockOrUnBlockMultipleContact`. Only the fields relevant to the route in question are read. The acting user always comes from the bearer token, never from this object.

kpostID.description: The user the address book belongs to. Overwritten from the bearer token on the V2 route.

deviceID.description: The device the address book was read from.

countryCode.description: Dial code used to normalise the imported numbers for matching against registered users.

phoneContacts.description: The address-book entries. Can be very large, so test against the request-size limit and establish whether the import is transactional or best-effort when one entry fails.

PhoneContactsRO.description: Device address-book import payload. **This carries bulk personal data about third parties who are not KPOST users and have not consented**, which makes it the most privacy-sensitive request object in the API - confirm the retention policy, whether numbers are hashed at rest, and what happens to it when the owning account is deactivated. On `POST /v2/contacts/importPhoneContacts` the owner is resolved from the bearer token; the V1 route takes it from this payload instead, with no ownership check.

countryID.description: Country of the mobile number, from `/v2/common/countries`.

mobileNumber.description: The number the OTP was sent to.

otp.description: The one-time code. Send this to verify; it is write-only from the client's perspective.

type.description: Which flow the OTP belongs to - registration, password recovery, device promotion. Confirm a code issued for one flow cannot be replayed against another.

expireDate.description: When the code stops being valid - a **10-minute** window on the send routes. Cover expiry explicitly in testing.

otpValidationStatus.description: Whether the code has been consumed. `N` until verified. A consumed code must not be accepted a second time.

OtpValidation.description: Mobile OTP record, used both to store a dispatched code and to submit one for verification. The OTP is **never returned in any response** - confirm that, and that it does not appear in application logs.

email.description: The address the OTP was sent to.

otp.description: The one-time code received by mail.

type.description: Which flow the OTP belongs to. Confirm cross-flow replay is rejected.

expireDate.description: When the code stops being valid.

otpValidationStatus.description: Whether the code has been consumed. `N` until verified.

EmailOtpValidation.description: Email OTP record, the email counterpart of `OtpValidation`. Used to store a dispatched code and to submit one for verification. The code is never returned in any response.

countryID.description: Country identifier, taken from `GET /v2/common/countries`. Determines the dial code and, on `sendOTP`, the applicable number-length rule.

mobileNumber.description: Mobile number in national format, digits only - no country code, spaces or punctuation.

requestType.description: Optional discriminator letting one payload serve several flows - for example distinguishing a registration OTP from a password-recovery OTP. Not validated at the controller layer; confirm the accepted values with the service.

companyID.description: Company identifier. Used only by `POST /v2/common/mobileNoExistInsideCompany`, which scopes the existence check to one organisation; ignored by the platform-wide routes.

MobileValidationRO.description: Mobile-number payload used by the OTP and number-existence endpoints in the Common module. Note that `POST /v2/common/sendOTP` applies an **additional country-specific length rule** on top of the bean validation below: India (`countryID` 1) requires exactly 10 digits and Malaysia (60) requires 7-8, so a number that passes validation here can still be rejected by that endpoint.

attachmentsUuid.description: The attachment UUIDs to verify. Each is checked independently and reported with its own numeric code in the response - `0` uploaded, `1` prefix created but no object, `2` nothing written, `3` not the caller's attachment.

items.description: The attachment UUIDs to verify. Each is checked independently and reported with its own numeric code in the response - `0` uploaded, `1` prefix created but no object, `2` nothing written, `3` not the caller's attachment.

kpostID.description: The owning user. Overwritten from the bearer token, so the check is always scoped to the caller's own namespace.

S3Attachments.description: Batch attachment-verification payload for `POST /v2/aws/checkAttachmentS3`, which confirms whether direct-to-S3 uploads actually landed before the UUIDs are referenced in a message.

prompt.description: The instruction for the model - what it should do with `message`.
prompt.example: Rewrite this to be more concise

message.description: The content being acted on. Concatenated after `prompt` before dispatch.
message.example: hey just checking whether we are still on for tomorrow

aiType.description: Selects the upstream provider. Defaults to `deepseek` when omitted.

sessionId.description: Existing conversation to continue. Omit to start a new session; the response returns the id to use on subsequent turns.

ChatRequest.description:
Prompt payload for the AI assistant at `POST /ai/chatResponse`. Note that `message` and `prompt` are **concatenated server-side** as `"<message>
 : <prompt>"` before being sent to the provider, so both contribute to the model input.

bearerAuth.description: JWT access token issued by the login endpoints. Format: `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.
